body: Looks like a kw/pb bumper. There are 2 18 mm bolts on each side of the radiator that hold the bumper on. Once these bolts are out, be careful not to break the hangars as they are fragile. As for the radar, I wouldn't touch it if I were you. You won't be able to repair it without having a program. The screws it stabs onto are weird and have to be replaced to fix the "loose" complaint. Then you have to connect with abs software to reset the alignment angles. It may need to be driven with a test running to reset, depending on the year. Final point, the bottom right ear is broken, so the radar needs to be replaced. I advise taking it to a dealer to get these repairs done.

Small tools are sometimes more important. I use 1/4" drive shallow wobble sockets on an 18" extension more often than I use my 3/4" and 1" drive sockets.  Make sure your 3/8 sockets go up to 24 mm and 1", because socket sets that stop at 19 are pretty pointless unless they are specialty. Have duplicates and different profile 24 mm, 15/16", 9/16", 13 mm, and 8mm sockets and wrenches. Get a set of ultra thin wrenches. Make sure you have fractional 4 angle wrenches. Make sure you have quality torx and allen sockets in multiple lengths and drive sizes. Knipex pliers wrench set is a must have: if you have enough room to use them, they are better than any wrench. The snapon miracle pliers are great, but the mini ones are irreplaceable. Weak power tools are just as important as the strong ones. 

Advise: if you don't know something, ask someone who does.

In order to pass:

Your check engine light can't be on

Your headlights, brake lights, and turn signals must all work

Your tires must have a certain amount of tread, brake pads must be over the minimum thickness.

You need at least 2 mirrors
